claim: The test calls its own mock instead of send_request_to_llm, so broken chat orchestration will still pass.
evidence: Lines 18–22 replace send_request_to_open_ai with llm_side_effect, and line 35 calls that replacement directly. The side effect supplies every asserted return value and appends the asserted history itself; the production send_request_to_llm never executes.

claim: The avatar-loader patch misses the imported reference, leaving the test dependent on the real application database.
evidence: Line 2 imports _load_avatar_infos_for_chat directly, while line 26 patches only chat_interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat. Line 33 invokes the original imported function, which opens TinyDB(DB_PATH) and calls avatar_page_settings.get without checking whether the settings record exists; an empty database therefore causes an AttributeError before the assertions.

claim: The new test requires undeclared pytest plugins and cannot run with the project's declared development dependencies.
evidence: The test requests the mocker fixture and uses pytest.mark.asyncio, requiring pytest-mock and pytest-asyncio. pyproject.toml declares only pytest and pytest-cov as development dependencies, and neither required plugin has a package entry in poetry.lock. A clean project installation cannot provide the mocker fixture.
